messages:
Tom - AE: Acme POC is hitting 401s intermittently when they swap projects. Can we swarm?
Customer - Acme Eng: Sending the failing request and decoded claim we see. Happens when we set X-Project-ID to `acme-ux-demo`.
Customer - Acme Eng: ```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk.prod.eyJhbGciOi...' 
 -H 'X-Project-ID: acme-ux-demo' 
 -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```
Customer - Acme Eng: Response: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid api key or token expired","request_id":"req_2263_a2"}`
Ivy (DevEx): Do we have the decoded JWT payload they pasted?
Customer - Acme Eng: payload: `{"sub":"svc-demo","org":"acme-intl","projects":["acme-main","acme-billing"]}` — note `acme-ux-demo` not present.
Ravi - Presales: Two possibilities: 1) token scope doesn't include the demo project, 2) token org claim (`acme-intl`) doesn't match routing org expected for that project (`acme-us`). Which model of binding do they use (org-first or project-first)?
Tom - AE: They said their infra forwards X-Org header too. But sometimes a CDN/proxy strips Authorization and retries with an edge key — causing mismatch. Could be a proxy rewrite.
Oncall (SRE Bot): Logged request req_2263_a2 -> route: us-west-2, worker-7, backend-v3. Error code AUTH_PROJECT_MISMATCH. Suggest verifying Authorization reaches origin.
Ivy (DevEx): Ask them to run `curl -v` and confirm Authorization header on the origin. Small snippet to decode JWT locally: `echo \"sk...\" | cut -d'.' -f2 | base64 -d` — check `org` and `projects` arrays.
Customer - Acme Eng: Verified header is present reaching origin. They then pasted a second request where the proxy added `X-Org: acme-us` while token org is `acme-intl`. Response: `403 project/org mismatch: token org acme-intl not allowed for project org acme-us`
Ravi - Presales: That explains it — our routing enforces org alignment unless token contains cross-org grants. For POC: options: a) mint a token with both org claims or with broad project list, b) change proxy to preserve original org header, or c) we issue an ephemeral org-bridged key.
Tom - AE: Customer asked if a single service key can be used across their orgs for demos. What's the policy?
Ivy (DevEx): We support multi-project tokens if org admin issues them. For production we recommend service accounts per logical org and short-lived tokens for cross-org access. I'll draft a short presales note.
Oncall (SRE Bot): Generated ephemeral token sk_ephemeral_2263 (expires 45m) scoped to `acme-ux-demo` and `acme-main`. request_id=req_2263_a3
Customer - Acme Eng: Re-tested with ephemeral token -> 200 OK, streaming chunks arriving. POC unblocked.
Ravi - Presales: Customer also asked about audit logs & rotation for ephemeral keys. I can include our key rotation cadence and link to audit log docs (SOC2 section).
Tom - AE: Follow-ups: 1) Help them update proxy to not rewrite org/project headers (Ivy to send config snippet), 2) capture steps so support KB shows `AUTH_PROJECT_MISMATCH` troubleshooting, 3) handoff security questionnaire answers to Ravi/Liz.
Ivy (DevEx): I'll add KB entry: checks (decode JWT, confirm Authorization at origin, compare org/project claims, issue ephemeral key). Will include sample curl and `jwt` decode commands.
Tom - AE: Thanks. I'll confirm final sign-off from customer and close thread. :white_check_mark:
